taxonomy.tagger_notes: The arc label in the prompt says 'East Blue Saga' but this chapter belongs to the Sabaody Archipelago Arc (part of the Summit War Saga). Character return tag set to true for Hatchan, a notable Fish-Man ally from the Arlong Park arc reappearing. Straw Hat count set to 8 (all post-Thriller Bark members: Luffy, Zoro, Nami, Usopp, Sanji, Chopper, Franky, Brook). Robin's absence from the summary is noted — she may be present but not mentioned; count kept at 8 to reflect confirmed presences. The revelation about Duval's face is the chapter's main cliffhanger/revelation moment.

title: Gaon Cannon
summary: Sanji and Duval argue about the face on Sanji's bounty poster, then Duval tells Sanji about his history. Afterwards, Duval shoots at Sanji with his harpoon gun in rage, but fails to hit him. He then orders two riders to drag Sanji into the water and drown him with a steel net. Camie leaps into the water and attempts to rescue Sanji. Meanwhile, the other riders attempts to use a giant anchor to sink the Thousand Sunny and drown the rest of the Straw Hat Pirates, especially those with Devil Fruit abilities. Franky, however, controls the ship and manages to escape the anchor with Chicken Voyage and then fights back with the Gaon Cannon, blasting away most of the riders. Duval's pet bison, Motobaro, attempts to attack the crew but is stopped by Luffy when he unintentionally uses Supreme King Haki. Duval then fights on his own and attempts to kill Sanji again with the harpoon gun, but Sanji evades them and starts to attack Duval's face. He then finishes Duval off with a very strong kick into the face.

taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le Gaon Cannon est une technique du Thousand Sunny, pas d'un personnage individuel — tagué comme nouvelle technique du chapitre. Le Haki du Conquérant de Luffy est utilisé involontairement sur Motobaro. Duval reçoit un flashback partiel expliquant sa haine envers Sanji (sa ressemblance avec le poster de prime). Zoro, Nami, Chopper et les autres membres de l'équipage sont mentionnés comme présents sur le Sunny mais n'ont pas d'actions déterminantes dans le résumé. L'arc est Sabaody Archipelago, précurseur de la Saga Amazon Lily, pas strictement East Blue Saga — le scraper indique 'East Blue Saga' mais le contexte suggère 'Sabaody Archipelago Arc' (Pre-Timeskip, Grand Line).

title: Yarukiman Mangrove
summary: The Takoyaki 8 crew prepares food for the Straw Hats. Duval comes to thank Sanji for re-constructing his face. Pappag explains to the Straw Hats how to get to New World. After the group arrives at Sabaody Archipelago, Hatchan warns the Straw Hats not to get involved with the World Nobles.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Pappag explique aux Straw Hats comment atteindre le New World via Sabaody Archipelago ; Hatchan les avertit de ne pas s'impliquer avec les World Nobles.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le résumé est très condensé pour ce chapitre. Duval est marqué comme character_return car il réapparaît après le Thriller Bark arc avec un nouveau visage refait par Sanji. La mention des World Nobles constitue une révélation majeure de lore pour l'arc Sabaody. L'arc Sabaody Archipelago débute officiellement ici. Brook est listé parmi les Straw Hats présents (9 membres à cette époque). Takoyaki 8 est une désignation de groupe (Hatchan, Camie, Pappag) et non un personnage individuel.

title: Adventure on the Archipelago of Dancing Soap Bubbles
summary: The Straw Hat Pirates happily explore Sabaody Archipelago until they encounter the Celestial Dragons.

taxonomy.revelation_description: The Straw Hats arrive at Sabaody Archipelago and encounter the Celestial Dragons (World Nobles), establishing the high-stakes social hierarchy of the location and the extreme danger of offending them.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: The résumé is very brief ('happily explore Sabaody Archipelago until they encounter the Celestial Dragons'), making precise tagging difficult. Chapter 497 is the introductory chapter of the Sabaody Archipelago arc. The Straw Hat crew present likely includes Luffy, Zoro, Nami, Usopp, Sanji, Robin, and Franky (Brook not yet confirmed joining at this point in continuity). Chopper is likely present but not mentioned explicitly — excluded to avoid invention. Sentomaru is not yet confirmed present in this specific chapter. Devil Dias is introduced as a slave of the Celestial Dragons. No explicit fight occurs in this chapter; the tension comes from the encounter with the World Nobles. Arc classification note: the scraper lists 'East Blue Saga' but Sabaody Archipelago is part of the Summit War Saga — this discrepancy is flagged.

title: The Incident of the Celestial Dragons
summary: Luffy angers the Celestial Dragons by attacking one, thus consequently summoning an Admiral to the Sabaody Archipelago.

taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le résumé est très court et synthétique. Luffy frappe le Celestial Dragon Charlos, déclenchant la convocation d'un Admiral (Borsalino/Kizaru). Hatchan est vraisemblablement blessé par Charlos avant l'intervention de Luffy selon le contexte du chapitre. Lacuba et Pascia sont des personnages mineurs présents dans la scène (esclave mermaid et acheteur). Eustass Kid est présent dans l'arc à ce stade mais son implication directe dans ce chapitre précis reste incertaine au vu du résumé minimal. straw_hats_count estimé à 3 (Luffy, Nami, Sanji visibles dans le contexte). Les tags devil_fruit_used sont inférés de l'attaque de Luffy sur Charlos. Confiance modérée due au résumé très bref.

title: Pirate Front Line on the Move!!
summary: News of the assault on the World Nobles quickly spreads around the Sabaody Archipelago. The other six Super Rookies immediately begin to escape the island before the admiral's arrival. In Mary Geoise, news arrives about the Celestial Dragon incident and an admiral volunteers to go to Sabaody Archipelago. Disco calls Donquixote Doflamingo for help, since the Human Auctioning House is owned by him, but Doflamingo tells Disco that slavery is old news and never to call him again. He also mentions that all of the Seven Warlords of the Sea are assembling for a great battle to come. Silvers Rayleigh frees Camie from her explosive collar. Luffy, Law and Kid battle against the Marines.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Doflamingo révèle que tous les Shichibukai sont convoqués pour une grande bataille à venir (préfiguration de la Bataille de Marineford). Il abandonne aussi le commerce d'esclaves, signalant un changement d'époque.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le Haki du Roi a été utilisé par Luffy dans ce chapitre (chapitre 504 marque une première manifestation notable). Borsalino/Kizaru est mentionné comme l'amiral qui se porte volontaire mais son apparition physique dans ce chapitre est probable mais non confirmée explicitement par le résumé. Doflamingo n'est présent que via Den Den Mushi. Les six autres Super Rookies fuient mais ne sont pas individuellement détaillés. L'arc mentionné (East Blue Saga) semble une erreur du scraper — ce chapitre appartient à l'arc Sabaody Archipelago (Summit War Saga).

title: Kuma
summary: Monkey D. Luffy, Eustass Kid, and Trafalgar Law fight off Marines. Law and Kid are revealed to be Devil Fruit users. Luffy, Law, and Kid emerge from the battle with the Marines, victorious. Kid states that Luffy, Law and Kid will meet up in the New World again, to which they agree on. Law invites Jean Bart to join his crew, the Heart Pirates to which Jean accept.

taxonomy.fight_winner: Monkey D. Luffy, Eustass Kid, Trafalgar D. Water Law
taxonomy.revelation_description: Law et Kid sont révélés comme utilisateurs de Fruits du Démon ; les trois capitaines se promettent de se retrouver dans le Nouveau Monde.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le résumé est succinct. La présence de Kuma (chapitre éponyme) et de Rayleigh, Borsalino, Sanji est inférée depuis le contexte de l'arc Sabaody (chapitres 500-513). Jean Bart rejoint les Heart Pirates de Law : alliance notable. Devil fruits de Law (Ope Ope no Mi) et Kid non nommé dans le résumé mais identifiés via le scraper. Arc indiqué 'East Blue Saga' semble erroné — Sabaody est dans le Grand Line/Archipel de Sabaody. Techniques Gear 3 mentionnées par le scraper. Kuma présent mais son rôle exact dans ce chapitre n'est pas détaillé dans le résumé.

title: Mushrooms-Grow-From-the-Body Mushroom
summary: Duval and the others are guarding the Thousand Sunny at Grove #41 waiting for the Straw Hats to return. At the auction house the marines try to calm an angry Shalria who is upset by the terrible condition her father and brother are in thanks to the Straw Hat Pirates. The marines assure her that admiral Kizaru will take care of things. Back at Shakky's bar, Camie expresses concern over the Straw Hats' safety. Hatchan assures her that their friends are strong and they will make it through this, but Shakky rebuts by saying that their friends are not strong enough to take on an admiral yet. Meanwhile Luffy finds himself on a mysterious island. He is determined to reunite with his crew. As he runs through the dense jungle Luffy recalls the moment he and his crew were separated, haunted by the fact that he was unable to save even one member of his crew. He then collides head on with a wall, knocking himself back and making him use his gigantic pistol to destroy it. Feeling drained, Luffy decides to feast on a random boar and some mushrooms. The mushrooms turn out to be poisonous and incapacitate Luffy as they grow all over his body. He is later found by members of the Kuja tribe and they take them back to their village to treat him mistaking him for a she. The Kuja tribe is able to successfully able to treat Luffy, but are shocked to later learn that he is of masculine origins having never seen a man before on the all female island of Amazon Lily.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Amazon Lily est une île peuplée exclusivement de femmes (les Kuja) qui n'ont jamais vu un homme auparavant ; Luffy y atterrit après la séparation de l'équipage.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le scraper inclut des lieux (Sabaody Archipelago, Human Auctioning House, Shakky's Rip-off Bar, Amazon Lily) et des objets (Thousand Sunny, Vivre Card) dans la liste des personnages, ce qui est inexact. Zoro, Brook, Nyon, Pappag, Rayleigh, Kuma, Rosward, Charlos et Bartholomew Kuma sont mentionnés contextuellement mais n'apparaissent pas physiquement dans ce chapitre. Marguerite est présente parmi les Kuja mais son nom n'est pas confirmé dans le résumé. La technique utilisée par Luffy contre le mur est probablement 'Gomu Gomu no Gigant Pistol' (Gear 3), mais cela n'est pas nommé explicitement dans le résumé. L'arc Amazon Lily commence officiellement ici.

title: Adventure on the Island of Women
summary: Luffy finally awakens and finds himself naked and in solitary confinement. As the citizens gather to see him, Kikyo tries to execute Luffy with her Haki imbued arrows. Luffy escapes his cell and avoids being recaptured. He decides to take Marguerite along with him for questioning. After escaping into the jungle, Luffy gets his Vivre Card back from Marguerite and learns that the empress of Amazon Lily is also a pirate.

taxonomy.tagger_notes: Boa Hancock est mentionnée comme impératrice et pirate mais ne semble pas apparaître physiquement dans ce chapitre — tagguée présente car référencée directement dans la révélation finale. Le Vivre Card est récupéré par Luffy — lié à l'objectif de retrouver son équipage.

title: Pirate Empress Boa Hancock
summary: While thinking of a way to get off Amazon Lily, Luffy attempts to find a way to travel but quickly learns that such is impossible for him. Suddenly, he is attacked by the women of the island, seeking to eliminate him as their empress has returned. Out at sea, Boa Hancock refuses to answer the call of the World Government to attend a Seven Warlords of the Sea meeting and instead turns the Marines into stone, with the exception of Vice Admiral Momonga, who tells her that if she does not answer the call, she will lose her Warlord status.

taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le chapitre établit deux scènes parallèles : Luffy piégé sur Amazon Lily et attaqué par les guerrières Kuja, et Hancock en mer refusant de répondre à la convocation du Gouvernement Mondial en pétrifiiant les Marines via le Mero Mero no Mi. Momonga se coupe la main pour résister à l'effet du fruit. Portgas D. Ace et Edward Newgate sont mentionnés dans le contexte de la convocation (guerre à venir) mais n'apparaissent pas physiquement dans ce chapitre. Le Haki n'est pas explicitement utilisé dans ce chapitre selon le résumé.

title: Bathing
summary: After returning from sea, Hancock is approached by Elder Nyon who asks her to reconsider the rejection of the World Government's call before being thrown out as Hancock prepares to take a bath. A pirate explains the history of Hancock and why everyone must not look at her when she removes her clothes due to a curse put on her. Meanwhile, Luffy looks for a ship to use and decides to see one on the tallest building, that building being the palace, the roof of which he crashes into and lands in Hancock's bathhouse, much to her wrath.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Explication de la prétendue malédiction de Hancock qui justifie que personne ne doit la regarder se déshabiller — couvre la vérité de sa marque d'esclave
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Aucun combat explicite dans ce chapitre. La 'wrath' de Hancock envers Luffy est une réaction émotionnelle, pas un combat formel. Le flashback mentionné est une explication narrative par un pirate sur la malédiction de Hancock, pas un flashback visuel canonique standard — tagué flashback_present=true car le passé de Hancock est évoqué. La marque d'esclave est implicitement liée à la Mero Mero no Mi mais le fruit n'est pas activé. Personnages comme 'Ran' et 'Enishida' sont des amazones de la garde rapprochée présentes dans ce type de scène.

title: The Arena
summary: Hancock, Marigold, and Sandersonia confront Luffy after the pirate broke into Hancock's bath and saw the mark on her back. Hancock uses her devil fruit to try to turn Luffy to stone, but it somehow does not work. Luffy is driven out of the palace, where he is captured by the Kuja Tribe and placed in an arena where he is to be executed. Marguerite, Sweet Pea, and Aphelandra try to defend Luffy, but Hancock turns them to stone and releases her executioner pet Bacura on Luffy. However, Luffy defeats Bacura with a single punch, and gets angry at Hancock and asks the crowd why they are cheering for her. Hancock replies that it is because she is beautiful, and tries to make Luffy fall for her charm, but fails again. She then sends Marigold and Sandersonia to kill Luffy, and they use their Devil Fruit powers to turn into snakes.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Hancock's Mero Mero no Mi has no effect on Luffy, suggesting his purity of heart or immunity to attraction-based powers
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Bacura est l'animal exécuteur de Hancock — son espèce exacte n'est pas spécifiée dans le résumé mais il est vraisemblablement un léopard noir selon le manga. Le Noro Noro no Mi listé par le scraper semble être une erreur — ce fruit appartient à Foxy et n'est pas pertinent ici. Les fruits du démon de Marigold et Sandersonia sont des Hebi Hebi no Mi modèles serpent (anaconda et king cobra) mais leurs noms exacts ne sont pas mentionnés dans le résumé. L'arc est celui d'Amazon Lily, faisant partie du Post-Enies Lobby / début de l'arc Impel Down, techniquement Grand Line (Calm Belt).

However, Luffy unwittingly stops them by unleashing Supreme King Haki, a one-in-a-million ability whose users are stated to have a king's disposition, and prepares to get serious in the fight.

title: Hoof of the Celestial Dragon
summary: Luffy is granted two choices: either free Sweet Pea, Marguerite, and Aphelandra from Boa Hancock's Mero Mero Mellow or he can get a ship and sail away, because he blocked Boa Sandersonia's slave symbol. He chooses to free them and is sent to the Kuja palace, where Boa Hancock shows him her slave symbol. After hearing from Nyon that Luffy assaulted a World Noble, Hancock, realizing she can trust him, tells him her shameful past as a slave and how she and her sisters were liberated by Fisher Tiger. When asked if Luffy hates her now that he knows she was a slave, Luffy says he does not and only hates the World Nobles and Hancock smiles stating she likes him and will give him a ship to get off the island.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Boa Hancock révèle qu'elle et ses sœurs ont été réduites en esclavage par des Nobles Mondiaux et portent la marque de Hoof of the Celestial Dragon ; elles ont été libérées par Fisher Tiger.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le Mero Mero no Mi est mentionné dans le contexte de la scène précédente (libération des guerrières pétrifiées) mais n'est pas activement utilisé dans ce chapitre. Fisher Tiger apparaît en flashback comme libérateur de Hancock et ses sœurs. Nyon est présente et joue un rôle informatif crucial en révélant à Hancock que Luffy a agressé un Noble Mondial. Le titre 'Hoof of the Celestial Dragon' fait référence à la marque d'esclave que portent Hancock et ses sœurs.

title: Fatal Illness
summary: Hancock promises Luffy a ship and decides to let him join the Kujas at a banquet. Luffy behaves as his usual self and parties with them as the Kuja marvel at Luffy's rubber body. As he eats they start poking and stretching him, angrily telling them he is not a side attraction and they give chase to him and Luffy runs away and escapes with Marguerite, who then thanks Luffy for saving her and her friends. They both arrive at Nyon's house where Luffy discovers Hancock's title of Warlord of the Sea, the war with the Whitebeard Pirates, and his brother's execution. Luffy asks for a way to save him and Nyon says only a Marine ship can make it to the prison he is at on time, Impel Down, and Hancock would have to use her title to make it. Luffy makes the tough decision to save his brother rather than to reunite with his crew. Nyon and Luffy see Hancock, who is revealed to have gotten sick and Nyon says she knows the sickness and tells her Luffy wishes to see her and Hancock does despite her illness. Luffy asks if she can board the Marine ship to save Ace, much to her sister's fury, thinking he is taking advantage of her. However, Hancock surprisingly agrees, much to her family's shock as Nyon says her disease is called "Love Sickness" and Hancock has fallen in love with Luffy.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Hancock a contracté la 'Love Sickness' en tombant amoureuse de Luffy ; révélation de la guerre imminente contre les Pirates de Whitebeard et de l'exécution prochaine de Portgas D. Ace à Impel Down ; Hancock accepte d'utiliser son statut de Shichibukai pour emmener Luffy sur un navire Marine.

Seuls Luffy, Hancock, Marguerite, Nyon et les Kuja sont physiquement présents. L'arc est techniquement Amazon Lily, sous-arc de l'arc Sabaody/Summit War. Le 'devil_fruit_used' est limité à Luffy dont le corps de caoutchouc est exploré par les Kuja (usage passif/démonstratif, non combatif). La décision majeure de Luffy de se rendre à Impel Down pour sauver Ace plutôt que de rejoindre son équipage est l'événement narratif central.

title: Hell
summary: Nyon helps explain to Hancock her Love Sickness and how it killed past empresses and if Hancock goes with Luffy she will survive and Hancock realizes her love for Luffy. Luffy and Hancock set off for the Marine Headquarters. Garp has traveled to Impel Down to speak with Ace, before his execution. Nami has been sent to a Sky Island called Weatheria. Franky has landed on an island where Vegapunk was born. Sanji has been sent to an Okama kingdom which he calls Hell.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Hancock réalise qu'elle est amoureuse de Luffy, ce qui explique sa Love Sickness. Nami se retrouve sur une Sky Island appelée Weatheria, Franky sur l'île natale de Vegapunk, et Sanji dans un royaume okama qu'il qualifie d'Enfer.

summary: Garp visits Ace in Impel Down and talks to him about the future he intended for him. Meanwhile, Boa Hancock approaches Impel Down with a hidden Luffy.

Buggy et Alvida sont listés par le scraper mais leur présence physique dans ce chapitre précis est incertaine selon le résumé fourni — ils sont inclus avec réserve. title: Adventure in the Great Prison
summary: Luffy and Hancock arrive at Impel Down and are greeted by Hannyabal and Domino. Luffy manages to sneak past the guards and proceeds down the prison's levels, meeting Buggy along the way.

summary: Hancock gives Luffy the key to Ace's handcuffs. As he runs off, Smoker tries to follow him but is blocked by the Pirate Empress. Meanwhile, Doflamingo tells Ivankov that Kuma recently lost all of his will as a human, becoming a weapon of the World Government. As Kuma attacks the pirates, Ivankov fights back. At the same time, Crocodile and Mr. 1 fight the Whitebeard Pirates. However, Jozu attacks Crocodile, forcing Doflamingo to intervene. Doflamingo suggests that the two team up, while Luffy runs into Mihawk.

Portgas D. Ace est présent mais apparaît de manière passive (remise de la clé). Les Fruits du Démon listés sont inférés depuis les personnages combattants connus (Hancock, Crocodile, Kuma). summary: Luffy tries to run past Mihawk, but is halted and forced back by the mighty swordsman, who cuts the gigantic frozen wave created by Aokiji in half. Buggy manages to dodge, but his bomb is deflected by Mihawk, giving Luffy an opportunity to escape. Mihawk pursues him, but is stopped by Vista. With the battle entering its final phase, Sengoku orders the cancellation of the Den Den Mushi signals, and Sentomaru appears with an army of Pacifista.

title: Oars' Path

summary: After Luffy's burst of Haki, Whitebeard orders his men to back him up. summary: Luffy and Ace, now free, fight their way through the Marine soldiers as Sengoku grumbles in disgrace. As his crew and allies look on in amazement, Whitebeard states that it is time to settle matters with the Marines.

Le titre 'The Times They Are A-Changin'' fait référence à la chanson de Bob Dylan, signalant un tournant dans la bataille de Marineford. Shichibukai présent via Doflamingo. L'arc est Marineford/Summit War, pas East Blue Saga — le scraper semble avoir mal catégorisé.

title: The Name of This Era is "Whitebeard"

Whitebeard est encore vivant dans ce chapitre (sa mort interviendra peu après). Le chapitre se concentre sur le sacrifice d'Ace pour protéger Luffy face à Akainu. Akainu moves to eliminate Luffy, but Marco comes to his aid and stops Akainu while Jinbe escapes with Luffy. An enraged Whitebeard attacks Akainu and knocks him into a huge fissure while simultaneously splitting Marineford into two pieces. However, Akainu manages to burn off a portion of Whitebeard's head. Just then, the Blackbeard Pirates arrive at the battlefield along with some new crew members, one of which is an immense figure the size of Marineford's main building. Sengoku and the Marines are stunned.

summary: Blackbeard arrives at Marineford with several new crew members. Whitebeard attacks, but Blackbeard and his crew gang up and attack the wounded pirate. Edward Newgate, the most powerful man in the world, dies standing up.

Roger' mais son nom n'apparaît probablement que dans le titre honorifique du chapitre ou une mention liée au statut de Whitebeard ; il n'est pas inclus comme personnage actif. La confiance est limitée par la brièveté du résumé.

title: Luffy and Ace

Le chapitre 582 appartient en réalité à l'arc post-guerre de Marineford. Les personnages listés par le scraper comme Edward Newgate, Gol D. Roger, Sakazuki, Monkey D. Garp peuvent être mentionnés dans le contexte du flashback ou du deuil mais ne sont pas confirmés physiquement présents selon ce résumé minimal.

The two of them hid, leaving Luffy still tied up. The Bluejam Pirates captured Luffy and interrogated him, but Luffy did not reveal the whereabouts of the money.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Sabo est introduit comme ami d'Ace et complice dans la cache du trésor volé aux Bluejam Pirates ; Luffy refuse de trahir ses frères malgré l'interrogatoire

La scène d'interrogatoire constitue une tension narrative mais pas un combat physique au sens strict. Curly Dadan et World Noble sont mentionnés dans le scraper mais n'apparaissent pas directement dans le résumé du chapitre.

title: Brothers' Sake Cups
summary: Sabo is revealed to be a Noble - a status he detests and the reason he had run away from home. However, Luffy and Ace do not care about Sabo's status, and the trio spend many happy days together. The three share sake cups and become sworn brothers. However, their days together are abruptly cut off when Bluejam, being paid by Sabo's father, forces Sabo to give himself up to his father in order to save Ace and Luffy.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Sabo est révélé être un noble de naissance, ayant fui sa famille aristocratique ; les trois frères (Luffy, Ace, Sabo) scellent leur fraternité par le partage des coupes de saké.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Ce chapitre est un flashback sur l'enfance de Luffy, Ace et Sabo dans le royaume de Goa. La révélation majeure est la noblesse de Sabo (fils d'Outlook III). Le pacte de fraternité est un moment charnière du lore. Bluejam agit comme intermédiaire coercitif au service du père de Sabo pour forcer son retour. Aucun combat direct n'est décrit, mais une coercition/menace est exercée par Bluejam. Le 'new_alliance_formed' reflète le serment des frères.

title: City of Stench
summary: Sabo returns to his parents' house by force and he meets his new adopted brother, Sterry. Meanwhile Ace and Luffy help the Bluejam Pirates distribute cargo throughout the Gray Terminal. Later Sterry gleefully reveals to Sabo that the King plans on burning down the trash at Gray Terminal, including all those that live there. It turns out the cargo from earlier was actually explosives, because Bluejam had supposedly struck a deal with the King in order to become a noble. That night the explosives are set off and Ace and Luffy end up trapped in the great blaze while Sabo desperately tries to get to them.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Le Roi de Goa planifie d'incendier le Gray Terminal pour nettoyer les déchets et ses habitants avant la visite d'un Noble Mondial ; la cargaison distribuée par Bluejam contenait en réalité des explosifs, et Bluejam avait passé un accord avec le Roi pour devenir noble.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Ce chapitre est un flashback centré sur l'enfance de Sabo, Ace et Luffy au Gray Terminal. Sterry est introduit comme frère adoptif de Sabo. Le Gouvernement Mondial est présent de manière indirecte via la mention d'un Noble Mondial (World Noble) dont la visite motive le nettoyage du Gray Terminal. Dragon et Ivankov sont listés par le scraper mais n'apparaissent pas physiquement dans le résumé de ce chapitre — ils ne sont donc pas inclus dans characters_present. La tension est très haute car Ace et Luffy se retrouvent piégés dans l'incendie en fin de chapitre.

title: I Will Not Run Away
summary: Bluejam corners Luffy and Ace. They are saved by the Dadan Family. Everyone runs except for Ace and Dadan who remain to face Bluejam. The residents of Gray Terminal are saved by Dragon and the Revolutionary Army. Sabo departs to become a pirate.

taxonomy.tagger_notes: Ce chapitre est un flashback du passé de Luffy à Fuusha/Goa Kingdom. Boa Hancock est Shichibukai donc shichibukai_present=true. Le plan entre Rayleigh et Luffy n'est pas explicité, d'où cliffhanger_type=mystery. Les personnages listés par le scraper incluant 'Amazon Lily', 'Sabaody Archipelago', 'Heart Pirates', 'Sea King', 'Boin Archipelago', 'Torino Kingdom', 'News Coo', 'Bartholomew Kuma' sont des lieux ou entités secondaires non confirmées physiquement présentes dans ce chapitre selon le résumé fourni. Jinbe et Nyon ont une présence probable à Amazon Lily mais non confirmée explicitement dans ce résumé.

title: Yell
summary: Zoro, Nami, Franky and Brook start their journey to return back to Sabaody Archipelago to reunite with Luffy.

taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le résumé est très minimal — il indique uniquement que Zoro, Nami, Franky et Brook commencent à retourner à Sabaody pour rejoindre Luffy. Le chapitre 592 fait partie de la période post-Marineford/post-timeskip annonce, où chaque membre de l'équipage est dans une île différente. Des personnages comme Perona, Mihawk, Gecko Moria, Haredas et Pekkori sont susceptibles d'apparaître selon le contexte de l'arc (présents dans les îles respectives des membres de l'équipage), mais leur présence exacte dans CE chapitre précis est incertaine au vu du résumé lacunaire. Dracule Mihawk est Shichibukai et est présent sur Kuraigana Island avec Zoro. Le scraper liste 'Sabaody Archipelago', 'Kuraigana Island', 'Weatheria', 'Karakuri Island', 'Namakura Island' comme lieux, ce qui suggère un chapitre montrant plusieurs membres en parallèle.

title: The Pledge
summary: The whereabouts of the other Supernovas are revealed, as well as the one defeated by Blackbeard. It is none other than Jewelry Bonney who was first kept as his prisoner, then arrested by the Marines after her captors flee. Both Chopper and Sanji decide to remain for some time on the islands they were sent to, in order to get stronger.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Jewelry Bonney fut capturée par Barbe Noire (Blackbeard) puis abandonnée et arrêtée par les Marines ; les positions et activités des autres Supernovas sont révélées
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le résumé est succinct. Le combat entre Blackbeard et Bonney est mentionné de manière implicite (elle est 'vaincue' et gardée prisonnière). Les Supernovas comme X Drake, Apoo, Law sont mentionnés comme ayant des positions révélées mais leurs activités précises ne sont pas détaillées dans le résumé. Doflamingo et Sakazuki apparaissent probablement dans le contexte politico-militaire (Mary Geoise/Gouvernement Mondial). Van Augur est listé par le scraper comme présent, probablement en tant que membre de l'équipage de Blackbeard lors de la scène avec Bonney. Ivankov apparaît dans le contexte de Kamabakka avec Sanji.

title: SPECTRUM
summary: Nami, Robin, Brook, Franky, and Usopp decide to work in their various environments in order to become better and stronger to help Luffy.
characters_mentioned: Legend of the Sacred Burning Beast of Baldimore

taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le résumé est très succinct. Le chapitre couvre plusieurs Mugiwara dans leurs environnements respectifs post-Marineford (arc d'entraînement de 2 ans). Luffy est mentionné comme motivation mais sa présence physique dans ce chapitre précis est incertaine — il est inclus car son retour au message aux nakama est la toile de fond de ces chapitres. Haredas (Weatheria) et Heracles (Boin Archipelago) sont des personnages secondaires présents dans ces lieux. Le chapitre est principalement de l'exposition/résolution émotionnelle liée à la décision des membres d'équipage de se former. Pop Green (arme d'Usopp) et le Legend of the Sacred Burning Beast of Baldimore (Karakuri Island / Franky) sont des éléments narratifs mais pas des personnages. Pirate King est un concept mentionné, pas un personnage. Vegapunk est mentionné en lien avec Karakuri Island.

title: <s>3D</s>2Y
summary: Zoro had defeated all the Humandrills but returned to Mihawk's castle and begged the Shichibukai to train him. Mihawk at first refused and was bewildered but agreed when he realized the reason was not for Zoro's own benefit. The swordsman revealed the message Luffy sent his crew members: the Straw Hat Pirates will reunite again in 2 years, after getting stronger. Meanwhile, Luffy started training with Rayleigh on Rusukaina Island and learned about the three forms of Haki.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Luffy a envoyé un message codé à tout l'équipage : les Straw Hats se retrouveront dans 2 ans après s'être entraînés séparément. Luffy commence également son entraînement avec Rayleigh et découvre les trois formes de Haki.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Ce chapitre marque le début du timeskip de 2 ans (arc de formation). Perona est mentionnée comme présente dans le contexte de Kuraigana Island mais son rôle actif dans ce chapitre n'est pas clairement détaillé dans le résumé. Le combat contre les Humandrills est présenté comme déjà terminé en début de chapitre. Mihawk accepte d'entraîner Zoro, constituant une nouvelle alliance/accord. Le Haki est mentionné comme enseigné par Rayleigh mais pas encore utilisé activement par les personnages dans ce chapitre.

title: 2 Years Later
summary: After 2 years spent training on islands around the world, the Straw Hat Pirates finally reunite at Sabaody Archipelago, which is now much more lawless due to the relocation of Marine Headquarters to the New World and because of the rise of a crew of fake Straw Hats, who are imitating the originals and recruiting members.

taxonomy.new_character_name: Fake Straw Hat Crew (Demaro Black as Fake Luffy, and associates)
taxonomy.revelation_description: Deux ans se sont écoulés depuis la séparation des Chapeaux de Paille ; le QG de la Marine a été déplacé vers le Nouveau Monde, rendant Sabaody plus anarchique, et un groupe de faux Chapeaux de Paille s'est constitué pour usurper leur réputation.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Ce chapitre est un chapitre de transition/introduction marquant le début du Post-Timeskip (Return to Sabaody Arc). Le résumé est succinct et ne détaille pas les apparitions individuelles des membres de l'équipage ni leurs actions précises. Boa Hancock est listée comme présente (probablement via Rusukaina/transport de Luffy) mais son rôle actif dans ce chapitre reste incertain. Les Faux Chapeaux de Paille sont introduits comme antagonistes secondaires. Les shichibukai_present est mis à true en raison de Boa Hancock. La liste des personnages détectés par le scraper est partielle — complétée avec les membres canoniques des Chapeaux de Paille et les faux membres. Le nombre straw_hats_count est estimé à 9 car le résumé indique une réunion complète mais Brook pourrait ne pas encore être arrivé à Sabaody dans ce chapitre précis.

title: Nine Pirates
summary: All of the Straw Hat Pirates have arrived at Sabaody Archipelago and begin to meet up at the Thousand Sunny. Luffy demonstrates his now controlled Haki on Fake Luffy. Franky demonstrates his new upgrade to Robin. Zoro gets on a departing pirate ship, intending to go fishing, and instead slices the ship in half, demonstrating some of his new skills in swordsmanship, commenting that he got on the wrong ship.

taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le chapitre marque la réunion de l'équipage après le timeskip de 2 ans. Boa Hancock et Sentomaru sont listés par le scraper mais ne sont pas confirmés présents dans le résumé fourni — non inclus dans characters_present. Demaro Black (Fake Luffy) est présent puisque Luffy utilise le Haki sur lui. Le Haki utilisé par Luffy semble être le Haki des Rois (Conqueror's Haki) pour soumettre Fake Luffy. Zoro coupe un navire en deux de manière comique (mauvais navire) — considéré comme démonstration de compétences plutôt que combat réel. Character_return = true car tous les membres réapparaissent après le timeskip de 2 ans.

characters_detailed.name: Demaro Black
characters_detailed.affiliation: Faux équipage de Chapeau de Paille

title:
Romance Dawn For the New World:
The Dawn of an Adventure
into a New World
summary: The Marines arrive and cause chaos on Grove 46 of Sabaody Archipelago. Sentomaru and his Pacifistas arrive to try to arrest the pirates. Monkey D. Luffy is revealed to the crowd, and is revealed to everyone that the real Straw Hat Pirates are alive. Luffy, Zoro, and Sanji then quickly leave for Grove 42 to start a new adventure in the New World.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Il est révélé publiquement que les vrais Straw Hat Pirates sont vivants, dissipant la confusion créée par les imposteurs
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le résumé est succinct. Brook est listé parmi les personnages détectés mais n'est pas explicitement mentionné dans l'action principale. Rayleigh et Shakuyaku sont probablement présents dans les cases mais non actifs. Les autres membres des Straw Hats (Nami, Usopp, Robin, Chopper, Franky) ne sont pas mentionnés — seuls Luffy, Zoro, Sanji sont confirmés actifs. Le combat implique principalement les Pacifistas/Sentomaru contre les pirates présents. L'arc se conclut (retour à Sabaody post-timeskip) et un nouveau s'ouvre (départ vers le Nouveau Monde).

title: Into the Depths
summary: As the Straw Hats venture deeper into the ocean, Nami, with some help from Franky and Brook, explains how different parts of the underwater current system work. Caribou﻿ and his crew try to attack the ship, but due to Momoo, becomes the only one of his crew to make it onto the ship. He pleads for his life and the crew ties him up. The chapter ends with the crew sighting the gigantic deep sea current, confronting a kraken, and Luffy planning to make the massive creature his pet.

taxonomy.tagger_notes: Edward Newgate listé par le scraper mais absent du résumé — non inclus comme présent. Caribou Pirates mentionnés collectivement mais seul Caribou monte réellement à bord. Momoo apparaît comme facteur accidentel dispersant les pirates de Caribou. Le 'combat' est davantage une tentative avortée d'abordage qu'un vrai affrontement. Arc taggé Grand Line (Fish-Man Island arc). La confrontation avec le kraken constitue le cliffhanger principal.

title: The Kraken and the Pirates
summary: The Straw Hats arrive at the Kraken, and Luffy aims to tame it. Usopp is startled by the Kraken and tries to convince Luffy to give up his ridiculous idea' Chopper mentions that the Kraken has likely been alive for hundreds of years, and is almost "mythological". Coribou's ship arrives from behind and is annihilated by the Kraken. Luffy, Sanji, and Zoro get lifesuits made from coating and set out to tame the beast. While the crew is dodging the Kraken, Luffy uses Gear 3 and hardens his enormous fist with Armament Haki, while Sanji and Zoro run interference with their respective strengths. Luffy blows away the Kraken with his gigantic fist, and a shark emerges from the Kraken. The crew, with Luffy, Sanji, and Zoro on the outside, get sucked into the trench and end up in the Underworld of the Sea.

taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le kraken (Surume) est soumis par Luffy à la fin du combat, ce qui constitue une alliance de facto — le combat se termine par une victoire/domination de Luffy. Megalo est listé par le scraper mais sa présence active dans ce chapitre est incertaine d'après le résumé ; inclus par précaution. Coribou est présent brièvement (son bateau est détruit). L'arc est Fish-Man Island/Fishmen Island qui fait partie de la New World Saga, mais le scraper indique 'East Blue Saga', ce qui est probablement une erreur du scraper — l'action se déroule clairement en route vers le Nouveau Monde (Grand Line/New World).

title: Deep Sea Adventure
summary: The crew continue their journey down. Usopp is seen calling for Luffy, Zoro and Sanji. The crew see jellyfish around the ship and one of them sticks their tentacle through the coating. Chopper tries to touch it, but is warned away by Robin. Franky uses the Coup de Burst to avoid a Sea King. Brook realizes that Caribou is missing. Caribou is shortly found and caught by Franky who locks him into a barrel. They are attacked by a Sea Devil only to be saved by captain Vander Decken. They turn on the Straw Hat Pirates realizing they are enemies; Luffy, Zoro, and Sanji come to their rescue having tamed the Kraken, whom Luffy named Surume.

taxonomy.tagger_notes: Robin warns Chopper away from the jellyfish tentacle, which counts as a morbid/dark warning remark. The 'Coup de Burst' is a Franky/Sunny technique previously introduced but named here in context; marked as new_technique_revealed with caution. Nami's presence is inferred as she is part of the crew on the Sunny but not explicitly mentioned in the résumé — included due to standard crew presence. Wadatsumi is listed in detected characters and appears alongside Vander Decken. Caribou's Numa Numa no Mi is referenced as he is caught escaping. The Kraken is tamed by Luffy, Zoro and Sanji and named Surume — this counts as a new alliance of sorts. Confidence slightly reduced due to partial résumé detail.

title: 10,000 Meters Under the Sea
summary: The Straw Hat Pirates and the pirates on the Flying Dutchman are escaping from the erupting volcano. As the other pirates, pulled by Wadatsumi and Ankoro, flee out of sight, the Straw Hats jump into a dark trench with Surume leading. They now fall, with an avalanche of stones following them that are getting closer to the Thousand Sunny. Right before being hit, Usopp saves the crew by using a Midori Boshi: Sargasso, growing seaweed on the cliff, catching most of the rocks. However, some rocks fall on the head of the Kraken, and they plunge into the deep sea, 10 000 meters below. Sanji, thinking of mermaids, almost faints. Being surrounded by enormous sea creatures, three fish-men come close. Luffy is asked to become a subordinate to the New Fish-Man Pirates, while Usopp fuels the tank to do Coup de Burst to Fish-Man Island. The chapter ends with Luffy turning down the offer.

locations: Deep Sea trench (10,000 meters under the sea)
taxonomy.tagger_notes: The scraper listed many characters not directly present in the narrative (Hatchan, World Noble, Fisher Tiger, Jolly Roger, Flying Dutchman crew). Only characters with confirmed on-page presence per the summary are tagged as present. Hammond, Hyouzou, and Kasagoba are identified as the three fish-men who approach the crew; their specific identities are inferred from knowledge of this arc. The arc is officially the Fish-Man Island Arc, but the scraper incorrectly lists 'East Blue Saga' — corrected contextually. No physical fight occurs; the confrontation is purely verbal/confrontational. Sanji's near-fainting from mermaid thoughts is treated as equivalent to nosebleed behavior characteristic of his character. Straw_hats_count is set to 3 as only Luffy, Usopp, and Sanji are explicitly named; other members are aboard the Sunny but not individually described.

title: Underwater Paradise
summary: The crew breaks through the bubble surrounding Fish-Man Island but get separated as a result. Luffy, Usopp, Sanji, and Chopper regain consciousness in Camie's apartment. Fish-Man Island's culture is further explained. The leader of the New Fish-Man Pirates orders his crew to bring the Straw Hats to him.

taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le scraper inclut des entrées non-personnages (Fish-Man Island, Devil Fruit, Yomi Yomi no Mi, All Blue, Noah) qui ont été filtrées. Arlong et Hammond sont mentionnés mais Hammond est le leader des New Fish-Man Pirates qui donne des ordres donc présent. Arlong semble mentionné dans le contexte culturel (passé) mais pas physiquement présent. Les membres séparés de l'équipage (Zoro, Nami, Robin) ne sont pas explicitement mentionnés dans le résumé donc non listés. Caribou est inclus car il était présent lors de la traversée. Sanji nosebleed est probable dans ce chapitre vu le contexte (île des sirènes) mais non explicitement confirmé dans le résumé — marqué avec réserve.

title: Adventure on Fish-Man Island
summary: Luffy, Sanji, Usopp, and Chopper spend time in Mermaid Cove. Luffy learns important information about Jinbe. The Neptune princes show up looking for Luffy. Luffy punches Hammond and his crew with jet pistol. Sanji suffers a nosebleed so severe he may die from it.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Luffy apprend des informations importantes sur Jinbe, ancien Shichibukai et ancien capitaine des Sun Pirates
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le scraper liste plusieurs éléments non-personnages (Mermaid Cove, Fish-Man Island, Ryugu Palace, etc.) ainsi que des personnages absents du présent narratif (Jinbe mentionné mais non présent physiquement, Fisher Tiger, Portgas D. Ace mentionnés dans l'information sur Jinbe). Hammond n'est pas listé par le scraper mais est clairement présent selon le résumé. Caribou est listé par le scraper mais n'est pas mentionné dans le résumé ; sa présence est possible (il est introduit à cette période de l'arc) mais non confirmée ici. La technique 'Jet Pistol' utilisée par Luffy est une technique connue, non nouvelle. L'arc correspond en réalité à l'arc Fish-Man Island (New World/Grand Line).

characters_detailed.name: Monkey D. Luffy
characters_detailed.power_used: Gomu Gomu no Mi — Jet Pistol

title: Hody Jones
summary: More of the New Fish-Man Pirates are introduced, while Luffy and his group arrive at Pappag's house and meet up with Nami. King Neptune makes his first appearance and invites Luffy and his crew to his palace, much to Camie and Pappag's shock. Back with the New Fish-Man Pirates, Hody Jones says that he will make everyone see that fish-men are the ultimate race.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Hody Jones révèle son idéologie suprémaciste : les hommes-poissons sont la race supérieure et il entend le faire reconnaître de tous.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le résumé mentionne 'Luffy and his group' sans préciser quels membres de l'équipage sont présents outre Nami et Brook — Chopper, Usopp, Robin, Zoro, Franky et Sanji pourraient être présents mais ne sont pas confirmés; seuls Brook et Nami sont clairement cités. Arlong et Fisher Tiger sont probablement mentionnés dans des dialogues d'Hody Jones comme références idéologiques plutôt que présents physiquement. Neptune est présenté comme nouveau personnage bien que roi de Fish-Man Island déjà évoqué. L'arc est Fish-Man Island (sous-arc de l'East Blue Saga dans certains découpages, mais narrativement dans le New World post-Timeskip).

title:
The Mermaid Princess
in Hard-Shell Tower
summary: Shirahoshi screams and yells for help, afraid that Luffy will hurt her. However, Luffy becomes her savior, as she has become a target of a large battle axe thrown at her from far away; Vander Decken IX has once again thrown a large weapon in her direction to try to kill her for not marrying him. Meanwhile, Zoro is arrested and the remaining three Straw Hats (Brook, Nami, and Usopp) take out guards who are trying to arrest them. As the guards falter one by one, Neptune takes a swing at them, but is stopped by Zoro, who had broken out of the palace prison to aid his friends. Back in the Fish-Man District, Hody Jones and Vander Decken IX make an alliance to take the head of Neptune.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Hody Jones et Vander Decken IX forment une alliance pour s'emparer de la tête du Roi Neptune
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Sanji absent du chapitre malgré son appartenance à l'équipage (non mentionné dans le résumé). Robin également absente. Le Fruit Mato Mato no Mi est utilisé par Vander Decken IX pour lancer la hache en direction de Shirahoshi. Wadatsumi est présent dans le Fish-Man District aux côtés de Hody Jones mais son rôle est mineur. L'arc est Fishman Island (erreur du scraper indiquant 'East Blue Saga').

title: What's Done is Done
summary: Zoro, Nami, Usopp, and Brook have tied up all the Ryugu Palace guards and King Neptune, and are now debating what their next course of action should be. The three princes arrive at what seems to be a hostage situation. Zoro negotiates with Fukaboshi, who reveals the contents of Jinbe's message to Luffy. Meanwhile, Luffy convinces Shirahoshi to go outside as it is her dream to see the Sea Forest.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Fukaboshi révèle à Zoro le contenu du message envoyé par Jinbe à Luffy, information cruciale pour la suite des événements à Fish-Man Island
taxonomy.tagger_notes: L'arc est Fish-Man Island (sous-arc de la Saga Île des Hommes-Poissons dans le Grand Line/New World entry), et non East Blue Saga comme indiqué dans le scraper — corrigé implicitement via sea_region. Jinbe est mentionné via son message mais n'apparaît pas physiquement ; il est tout de même listé dans characters_present car son message est central à la scène. Les Medaka Mermaid Quintuplets ne sont pas mentionnées dans le résumé et n'ont pas été incluses. Le titre 'What's Done is Done' reflète la résignation de Neptune face à la prise d'otages accomplie.

title: Mato Mato Curse
summary: Luffy and Shirahoshi start heading for the Sea Forest. Brook tells everyone about the invasion. Jones and Decken are shown preparing for the invasion.

taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le résumé est très court et peu détaillé. L'arc est listé comme 'East Blue Saga' mais le chapitre 615 appartient à l'arc Fish-Man Island (sous l'arc Fishman Island de la saga New World / Fish-Man Island Saga). La liste des personnages du scraper inclut des lieux (Coral Hill, Ryugu Kingdom, Fish-Man Island, Noah) et des concepts (Energy Steroid) comme personnages — ignorés pour les tags. Arlong, Otohime et Jinbe sont mentionnés dans le contexte de l'arc mais ne semblent pas physiquement présents dans ce chapitre selon le résumé. Le titre 'Mato Mato Curse' (Mato Mato no Mi) suggère que le Fruit du Démon de Vander Decken IX est mentionné ou au moins implicite, mais aucune utilisation explicite n'est décrite dans le résumé.

title: Major Incident on Coral Hill
summary: Zoro prepares to fight Hody after helping Neptune, his guards, Usopp, and Brook escape. Nami has disappeared to an unknown location after seeing Hody has an Arlong tattoo. At Coral Hill, Luffy, Megalo, and Shirahoshi meet Chopper, Sanji, and Hatchan. Megalo finally spits out Shirahoshi.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Nami discovers that Hody Jones bears an Arlong tattoo, connecting him to the Arlong Pirates that once enslaved her village
taxonomy.tagger_notes: The résumé is brief; Arlong is mentioned contextually via his tattoo on Hody Jones rather than as a physical presence — he is not counted as physically present. Vander Decken IX is listed by the scraper but absent from the résumé narrative; he is included in characters_detailed with minimal tags. Neptune and his guards escape alongside Usopp and Brook. The arc label 'East Blue Saga' appears erroneous for chapter 617 which belongs to the Fish-Man Island Arc (New World portion of the Grand Line); sea_region set to Grand Line accordingly.

title: Otohime and Tiger
summary: A flashback to sixteen years ago, showing Otohime's compassion for the citizens and trying to get a petition signed to show, during Levely, that fish-men want to live above the surface of the sea. The creation of the Sun Pirates and Jinbe's and Arlong's involvement are explained.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Origine des Sun Pirates expliquée — Fisher Tiger, Jinbe et Arlong y appartiennent. La pétition d'Otohime pour que les hommes-poissons puissent vivre en surface et participer au Levely est détaillée, révélant les motivations politiques et sociales de l'arc.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le chapitre est entièrement en flashback (seize ans avant le présent narratif). Fisher Tiger est mentionné comme fondateur des Sun Pirates, dont font partie Jinbe, Arlong et Macro. Edward Newgate est mentionné comme protecteur de l'île des hommes-poissons. Jinbe deviendra Shichibukai — au moment du flashback il ne l'est pas encore, mais il est tagué shichibukai_present=true car c'est sa période de formation. Otohime porte la pétition pour le Levely afin que les hommes-poissons/sirènes puissent vivre en surface. L'assaut de Fisher Tiger sur Mary Geoise est mentionné comme contexte. Le scraper listait des non-personnages (Firearm, Blue Planet, etc.) qui ont été ignorés.

title: The Sun Pirates
summary: The Sun Pirates become more and more of a threat, gaining infamy on the surface and fame on Fish-Man Island. They then meet a former slave girl named Koala, who was at first afraid of being killed due to enslavement, but then started crying due to Tiger's words of encouragement.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Les Sun Pirates sont présentés dans leur montée en puissance, et on découvre leur rencontre avec Koala, une ancienne esclave humaine libérée, et les valeurs humanistes de Fisher Tiger.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Ce chapitre est entièrement inscrit dans le flashback de l'arc Fish-Man Island, centré sur l'histoire des Sun Pirates. Le scraper liste de nombreux personnages (Hody Jones, Dosun, Zeo, Daruma, Ikaros Much, Neptune, Otohime, Shirahoshi, Borsalino, Marines, etc.) qui sont sans doute présents ailleurs dans l'arc mais pas nécessairement dans ce chapitre spécifique selon le résumé fourni. Seuls Fisher Tiger, Koala, Jinbe, Arlong et Hatchan sont confirmés par le résumé. La localisation exacte reste la surface de la mer dans un contexte de flashback.

title: Fisher Tiger the Pirate
summary: The Sun Pirates eventually reach Koala's hometown, where unfortunately they are ambushed by marines who were waiting for them. Fisher Tiger manages to escape, injured, on a stolen marine ship, but he dies there because he refused to take human blood. Enraged because of his death, Arlong goes back to Koala's hometown to take revenge on the marines, but is captured by Vice Admiral Borsalino.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Fisher Tiger meurt en refusant une transfusion de sang humain après l'embuscade des marines, révélant la profondeur de sa haine/idéologie contre l'oppression humaine.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le chapitre est un flashback sur l'arc Fisher Tiger/Sun Pirates. La mort de Tiger est annoncée (hors champ direct — il meurt sur le navire après s'être échappé), classée comme offscreen. Borsalino (futur amiral Kizaru) capture Arlong, impliquant un affrontement mais le résumé ne précise pas s'il utilise son Fruit du Démon explicitement dans ce chapitre ; devil_fruit_used mis à false par prudence. Strawberry est un Vice-Admiral présent dans ce contexte mais peu détaillé dans le résumé.

title: Queen Otohime
summary: Following Fisher Tiger's death, Arlong is captured and jailed by Borsalino. Jinbe receives an invitation to join the Shichibukai. By doing so, he receives a pardon for every member of the Sun Pirates, including Arlong. Arlong is angered by Jinbe's decision, resulting in him seceding to the Arlong Pirates along with many others. Meanwhile, citizens of Fish-Man Island begin retracting their signatures from Queen Otohime's petition. This upsets her to the point of making a drunken announcement asking for everyone to broaden their horizons and seek unity between fishpeople and humans alike. Shortly after, news of a wrecked ship reaches the island and that a World Noble is on board. Queen Otohime rushes to help.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Jinbe rejoint les Shichibukai, ce qui libère les membres des Sun Pirates y compris Arlong, qui fait alors sécession pour fonder les Arlong Pirates.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le chapitre est un flashback narratif sur la période post-mort de Fisher Tiger. Borsalino capture Arlong (combat implicite/off-panel). Jinbe rejoint officiellement les Shichibukai. La scène d'Otohime ivre et sa réaction à l'annonce du naufrage d'un Celestial Dragon constituent le cliffhanger. Plusieurs personnages listés par le scraper (Hatchan, Hody Jones, Neptune, Shirahoshi, princes, etc.) ne sont pas explicitement présents dans le résumé et ne sont donc pas inclus dans characters_present.

title: Uninherited Will
summary: The destroyed ship of a Celestial Dragon reaches the main gate of Fish-Man Island. Mjosgard, the only survivor, demands the people bring him a mask. But the citizens along with some of the Sun Pirates refuse while a member of the Sun Pirates tries to shoot Mjosgard but Otohime gets in the way and takes the bullet. Meanwhile, Shirahoshi shows that she possesses the power to call upon Sea Kings and that is why Vander Decken IX showed interest in her the first time. The World Noble is healed by Aladine a few weeks later and Otohime chooses to go with the noble to the surface for a week. She returns with an important document.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Shirahoshi possède le pouvoir d'appeler les Sea Kings, ce qui explique l'intérêt initial de Vander Decken IX pour elle — révélant qu'elle est l'Arme Ancienne Poseidon.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Ce chapitre est un flashback sur l'arc Fish-Man Island, racontant des événements passés de l'île. Shirahoshi est implicitement révélée être Poseidon (Arme Ancienne) via son pouvoir sur les Sea Kings — ancient_weapon_mentioned=true. Otohime se sacrifie pour protéger Mjosgard d'une balle tirée par un Sun Pirates, mais ne meurt pas dans ce chapitre (sa mort survient plus tard dans le flashback). L'affrontement est limité à une tentative de tir et une interposition. Jinbe et Fukaboshi sont mentionnés/présents comme membres des Sun Pirates et famille royale respectivement. Aladine soigne Mjosgard, ce qui est son rôle médical habituel.

title: The Three Neptune Brothers
summary: Otohime's goal of joining the humans comes to fruition. She explains Shirahoshi's ability to her sons. When she is collecting signatures, she is assassinated.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Otohime révèle à ses fils la véritable nature du pouvoir de Shirahoshi : sa capacité à communiquer avec les Rois des Mers (Voice of All Things / Poseidon). Elle est ensuite assassinée alors qu'elle collectait des signatures pour son projet de rapprochement entre humains et poissons-hommes.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le résumé est très bref. Le chapitre est entièrement en flashback (le passé de Fish-Man Island). La mort d'Otohime est présentée comme survenant dans ce chapitre mais dans le cadre du flashback, donc character_death_present et character_death_flashback sont tous deux à true. Shirahoshi est identifiée implicitement comme l'Arme Ancienne Poséidon via la révélation de son pouvoir de communiquer avec les Rois des Mers, d'où ancient_weapon_mentioned=true. Neptune est probablement présent mais son rôle n'est pas explicitement mentionné dans le résumé. Vander Decken IX peut apparaître brièvement. Le scraper mentionnait 'World Noble' mais le résumé ne le confirme pas directement dans ce chapitre précis.

characters_detailed.name: Shirahoshi
characters_detailed.power_used: Voice of All Things / Poseidon — capacité à convoquer les Rois des Mers

title: Former Warlord in the Way
summary: Luffy continues his fight with Jinbe because he wants to deal with Hody alone. Robin appears in the middle of the fight, surprising everyone, throwing them off. Meanwhile, Jones starts to move residents from the Fish-Man District to the island. In Candy Factory Town, Daruma says that he will gather everyone at Gyoncorde Plaza. In Ryugu Palace, inside the pool area, Zoro, Usopp, and Brook are still trapped and try to find a way to escape with Brook's new ability.

taxonomy.tagger_notes: Jinbe was a former Shichibukai at the time of this arc, hence shichibukai_present=true. Brook's 'new ability' is referenced but not named explicitly in the summary, so new_technique_revealed remains false. Sanji, Chopper, and Pappag are listed as detected by the scraper but not mentioned in the summary body — their presence is uncertain; they may appear briefly. Arlong, Hatchan, and the New Fish-Man Pirates are factions/characters referenced contextually but not shown acting in this chapter. The arc is Fishman Island Arc, not East Blue Saga — the scraper's arc label appears erroneous.

title: Getting Violent
summary: Dosun has been captured and is guarded by civilians, but due to energy steroids he breaks free. Before the Fish-Man's Meeting hall, some of the New Fish-Man Pirates try to make a drunken Hyouzou go to the plaza. Zeo is trampled on the ground, but still threatens and orders the civilians around. The three princes are heading to the Gyoncorde Plaza. In the Gyoverly Hills, the sea bear is ravaging the place and everyone, including the left and right ministers and even the New Fish-Man Pirates, are afraid and want to calm it with fire, but Ikaros stops them and gets angry, since fire dries him out. Hody Jones arrives at the plaza only for his crew to see him suffering from an Energy Steroid overdose.

taxonomy.tagger_notes: Jinbe est listé comme détecté par le scraper mais n'apparaît pas explicitement dans le résumé — non inclus dans characters_present. Shyarly et Neptune apparaissent probablement dans ce contexte (Mermaid Cove mentionné) mais leurs actions ne sont pas décrites dans le résumé. Jinbe est un ancien Shichibukai, sa présence n'est pas confirmée ici, mais le tag shichibukai_present est mis à true pour Jinbe s'il est présent hors-résumé — conservé avec réserve. La sea bear ravageant Gyoverly Hills est un élément comique/tendu mais pas un combat au sens strict entre personnages nommés. Hody's Energy Steroid overdose constitue le cliffhanger principal.

title: Gyoncorde Plaza
summary: Decken is left heartbroken by Shirahoshi's words and gets an idea. At the Gyoncorde Plaza, Neptune's army is defeated and the entrance to the plaza was barricaded so no one interrupts the execution. Hody's appearance changes and he becomes very powerful. The three princes arrive at the scene, defeat all of the sea beasts and run at the New Fish-Man Pirates's officers while Shirahoshi, Jinbe and Megalo hurry to the plaza.

taxonomy.tagger_notes: Jinbe est encore officiellement Shichibukai à ce stade de l'arc. Hody Jones prend des Energy Steroids qui transforment son apparence, ce qui pourrait être considéré comme une transformation/power-up mais n'est pas un Fruit du Démon. Luffy est présent dans le chapitre mais son rôle actif reste limité au déplacement vers le plaza. La liste du scraper incluait des lieux et des objets (Gyoncorde Plaza, Energy Steroids, Mermaid Cove, Gyoverly Hills, Queen Otohime) filtrés de la liste des personnages. Queen Otohime n'apparaît pas physiquement dans ce chapitre. L'arc est Fish-Man Island et non East Blue Saga.

title: I Knew
summary: The princes are defeated and are up for execution with their father. Also Shirahoshi and Jinbe fall enchained from the sky, to which Hody Jones reacts glad, saying that it must be his lucky day. Madam Shyarly shows up in the crowd and tells Hody that he will not reign the country, as Luffy will destroy all of it. Enraged by this, he shoots Shyarly down with a Water Shot and pleads to her that her brother is far different from himself. He then goes on, telling the whole island that he assassinated Queen Otohime, to which everyone reacts surprised. Meanwhile, Vander Decken IX has thrown the ship Noah toward Shirahoshi.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Hody Jones révèle publiquement devant tout Fish-Man Island qu'il a assassiné la reine Otohime
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Luffy est mentionné par Shyarly (sa prédiction le concernant) mais sa présence physique dans le chapitre n'est pas clairement confirmée par le résumé — il est possible qu'il soit absent physiquement. Otohime apparaît uniquement par la révélation de son assassinat, pas en flashback direct. Noah est un bateau, non un personnage — retiré de characters_detailed. Gyoncorde Plaza et Fish-Man District sont des lieux, non des personnages. New Fish-Man Pirates et Flying Pirates sont des groupes présents en arrière-plan. Water Shot est une technique nommée utilisée par Hody Jones. Le scraper a inclus des lieux et des groupes comme personnages — corrigé.

characters_detailed.name: Vander Decken IX
characters_detailed.power_used: Mato Mato no Mi (ciblage de Noah sur Shirahoshi)

title: Friend or Foe
summary: Shirahoshi reveals that she knew the truth behind her mother's death because Megalo witnessed the murder at the time, and relayed the information to her. Hody Jones is about to land the finishing blow on king Neptune, when Luffy jumps out of Megalo's mouth at that moment and attacks him. Above the plaza are the Thousand Sunny and Neptune's whale, Hoe. The Sunny blasts the majority of fish-man pirates with the Gaon cannon, while the whale rescues his master. It turns out that this rescue was planned out by Jinbe. The island residents ask Luffy if he is a friend or foe, to which he responds that it's their call to make. The rest of the crew then gather at the plaza, and are prepared to engage Hody's crew in combat alongside Jinbe.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Shirahoshi reveals she knew the truth of her mother Queen Otohime's murder because Megalo witnessed it and told her — explaining why she kept it secret all along.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: The Gaon Cannon has been shown before in Sabaody but this may be its first named/featured use in combat context — tagged as new_technique_revealed with caution. The Straw Hats count is set to 2 (Luffy and Franky visible; Robin is also mentioned as gathering at the plaza, so count is 3). Correcting straw_hats_count to 3 (Luffy, Robin, Franky). The alliance between Jinbe/Straw Hats and the Ryugu Kingdom is forming. Shyarly and Fukaboshi appear peripherally. The chapter title 'Friend or Foe' references Luffy's answer to the islanders. Arc label in the prompt says 'East Blue Saga' but this is clearly the Fish-Man Island Arc (Grand Line / New World).

title: The Ancient Ark
summary: Luffy's strength is overwhelming Hody Jones leaving everyone observing amazed at his power. He uses Haki to attack Hody, however Hody is very resilient, and gets back up. Noah is seen arriving at Fish-Man Island with Vander Decken IX onboard. As the ark nearly breaks through the bubble surrounding Fish-Man Island, Shirahoshi leaves the plaza to draw the ark away. She stands in front of Decken as she asks him to only kill her and leave the island alone. Hody is then seen climbing on one of the chains at the bottom of the ark, looking furious. Sanji then quickly runs to Noah, but Luffy stops him and decides to head to Noah himself.

taxonomy.tagger_notes: Shirahoshi est Poseidon (arme ancienne), ce qui justifie ancient_weapon_mentioned=true. Le Haki utilisé par Luffy est implicitement de l'Armement (Busoshoku) pour frapper Hody. L'arc est Fish-Man Island, qui appartient techniquement à la Grand Line (Paradise). Jinbe et Wadatsumi sont mentionnés comme observateurs mais le résumé ne décrit pas leurs actions directes. L'arc East Blue Saga dans les métadonnées semble erroné — Fish-Man Island est un arc de la Grand Line (post-Time Skip).

title: Escape-Hoshi
summary: Shirahoshi runs away from Noah trying to get outside of Fish-Man Island to save the bubble around it. Luffy is sent flying toward the ark with Sanji's help. Inhabitants of Fish-Man Island try to slow the arc down by pushing and pulling it, but Hody Jones disposes of them for being worthless. Then Shirahoshi manages to get out of Fish-Man Island and continues to lure the ship out, as Luffy and Hody follow her and Hody sees a chance to kill him. Shirahoshi refuses another one of Decken's proposals and is saved from his attack by her brothers and Hoe while Fukaboshi saves Luffy. Hody tries to attack them with his Kirisame, but it misses so then he gets on Noah and impales Decken with his trident.

taxonomy.tagger_notes: Le chapitre est centré sur la fuite de Shirahoshi hors de Fish-Man Island pour attirer Noah à l'extérieur de la bulle protectrice. Noah est un lieu/objet central mais pas un personnage. Kirisame est une technique de Hody Jones utilisée ici (attaque manquant sa cible). Hody impale Decken avec son trident à la fin — Decken est blessé mais pas confirmé mort. L'arc est Fish-Man Island (pas East Blue Saga, le scraper se trompe d'arc). Sanji est présent brièvement pour propulser Luffy. Neptune est mentionné implicitement via les princes mais sa présence directe dans ce chapitre n'est pas confirmée par le résumé — conservé avec réserve.

characters_detailed.name: Shirahoshi
characters_detailed.power_used: Capacité d'Ancient Weapon Poseidon (appel des Sea Kings implicite / attraction de Noah)

title: What Are You?
summary: Noah is on a collision course with Fish-Man Island and after Fukaboshi explains Luffy in a short flashback about the importance of Noah, he wants to smash it, but is stopped. Shirahoshi asks Decken to wake up. After Hody sends a hard blow to Manboshi, Luffy gets on him and punches Hody. He gets away and fights for a short while with Fukaboshi and then he defeats him. In the meantime, Luffy gets contacted by the fish-men he met awhile back, telling him that they can launch the bubble around Noah for Luffy to fight inside. While Hody attacks Luffy again, Luffy breaks his Kirisame and punches him back. Fukaboshi contacts him with a Den Den Mushi and tells him, that he knows Hody's "true motive".

taxonomy.revelation_description: Fukaboshi révèle à Luffy qu'il connaît le véritable mobile de Hody Jones
taxonomy.tagger_notes: L'arc est Fish-Man Island (sous Grand Line/New World), non East Blue — le scraper indique incorrectement East Blue Saga. Poseidon (Shirahoshi) est mentionnée implicitement comme arme ancienne via Noah. Hody bat Fukaboshi (fight_winner=Hody), mais son combat avec Luffy n'est pas conclu. Fukaboshi révèle le 'vrai motif' de Hody en cliffhanger via Den Den Mushi. Les fish-men alliés proposent une bulle autour de Noah pour que Luffy se batte à l'intérieur — nouvelle stratégie notable. ancient_weapon_mentioned=true car Shirahoshi est Poseidon et Noah est lié à son pouvoir.

title: Phantom
summary: While the Neptune army is fighting the New Fish-Man Pirates, Robin frees the slaves. Then she gets captured by Hammond with a net, but still defeats him by making two clones. Zeo crawls to Brook, but Brook hears him and stops his sneak attack. He explains his powers and then attacks Zeo again. Usopp dodges Daruma's charge and tells him why he cannot lose. The Ammo Knights from the Air Tank contact Neptune and he grants them the use of the national Den Den Mushi. With that they tell the people that Noah is on a collision course with Fish-Man Island and they are to evacuate. Then there is a lot of static during a short conversation between Luffy, Shirahoshi, and the knights. Fukaboshi reveals what Hody Jones is, that he is a monster created from a grudge of the fish-man race against the humans.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Fukaboshi révèle que Hody Jones est un monstre né de la rancœur de la race des poissons-hommes contre les humains, sans avoir vécu lui-même de tragédie personnelle.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Robin utilise son Hana Hana no Mi pour créer deux clones et vaincre Hammond. Brook détecte Zeo grâce à son ouïe et le contre. La grande révélation de Fukaboshi sur la nature de Hody Jones (produit de la haine abstraite, sans trauma personnel) est le moment narratif majeur du chapitre. L'arc de Luffy/Shirahoshi sur Noah est évoqué brièvement avec des parasites sur la transmission. Hody Jones est mentionné mais n'apparaît pas directement dans l'action.

title: To Zero
summary: Noah continues falling toward Fish-Man Island while a flashback of Hody's appears. In the Fish-Man District, Hody and the New Fish-Man Pirates officers were taught as children that the humans are an inferior species and they should be punished by heaven. The flashback moves forward in time when Hody was a Neptune Army member and he and his crew commit crimes, celebrate the death of Otohime, and start producing Energy Steroids and the flashback ends. Fukaboshi gives an emotional speech to the whole island about the cause of this event and begs Luffy to create a new beginning. Luffy then tells Fukaboshi to leave everything to him and his crew. After the discussion ends, Hody catches up to Luffy and Shirahoshi and Luffy punches him through the chest with a new Haki imbued punch.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Révélation que Hody Jones et les officiers des Nouveaux Pirates des Hommes-Poissons n'ont pas vécu de traumatismes directs causés par les humains — leur haine est héritée d'un enseignement idéologique reçu dans le District des Hommes-Poissons, et non d'une expérience personnelle.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Silvers Rayleigh et Fisher Tiger sont mentionnés dans le résumé du scraper mais n'apparaissent pas dans le résumé narratif du chapitre — ils ne sont pas tagués comme présents. Otohime apparaît en flashback (sa mort est évoquée mais pas montrée explicitement comme une mort dans ce chapitre). La nouvelle technique (coup de poing imbué de Haki) n'est pas nommée explicitement dans le résumé, donc new_technique_revealed=false. Le combat Luffy vs Hody est en cours mais ne se conclut pas dans ce chapitre.

characters_detailed.name: Monkey D. Luffy
characters_detailed.power_used: Haki d'Armement (coup de poing à travers la poitrine de Hody)

title: A Voice From the New World
summary: Luffy, Zoro, and Sanji find Caribou knocked out, take all of the treasure and head back to the palace. On their way they meet the Minister of the Left while he is being threatened by Pekoms. Luffy accidentally reveals that he ate candy at the banquet and is soon questioned by Mr. Pekoms on that. Baron Tamago stops Pekoms and starts explaining the situation calmly to Luffy. On Whole Cake Island, Big Mom is very eager to eat the sweets from Fish-Man Island. Bobbin, one of her pirates, returns and reveals that he destroyed a country for not being able to pay their tribute of sweets in time as she requested. She uses a Den Den Mushi to call Fish-Man Island, which Luffy answers and tells her there is no more candy, lying that he ate all of it. He tries to negotiate by offering all of the treasure, but fails despite Tamago encouraging the deal due to the pirate group being low on cash. Big Mom does agree to direct her anger towards Luffy and not Fish-Man Island, and Luffy declares war on her, saying he will make Fish-Man Island his territory.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Luffy declares war on Big Mom (Charlotte Linlin), a Yonko, and claims Fish-Man Island as his territory. Bobbin reveals Big Mom destroyed a country for failing to pay tribute in sweets.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: The arc listed as 'East Blue Saga' appears incorrect for chapter 651, which belongs to the Fish-Man Island Arc (New World). character_death_offscreen is set to true for the unnamed country destroyed by Bobbin on Big Mom's orders, though no named individual died. No physical combat occurs but there is significant confrontation/tension. Straw Hats count set to 3 (Luffy, Zoro, Sanji) as the only confirmed present members. Franky, Chopper, Usopp detected by scraper but not confirmed present in the summary. Eustass Kid and Garp mentioned by scraper but not present in the chapter summary.

title: Grim Premonitions
summary: Jinbe and Neptune have a discussion at Ryugu Palace about cutting off their connections to Big Mom and Neptune has found the flag he would wish to use to defend his island in case he loses Big Mom's, the flag of the Straw Hat Pirates. The Minister of the Right comes and alerts Neptune that there is a bomb inside the Tamatebako that will explode when the box is opened. Luffy returns to the palace and tells everyone that he gave all the treasure he collected from Caribou to Big Mom and that he would fight her. In consequence, everyone is shocked and Luffy, Zoro and Sanji get beaten up by Nami. Caribou wakes up and tries to find the treasure he stole. He sees that Pekoms has it and tries fighting him only to be defeated with one punch. In the New World, the pirates that just escaped from Hody Jones' slave army are attacked by the Marines. On a Marine battleship, Smoker is interrogating some captured pirates who tell him that the one who saved them was Luffy.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Le Tamatebako contient une bombe qui explose quand la boîte est ouverte ; Neptune envisage de se placer sous la protection des Chapeaux de Paille plutôt que de Big Mom.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: Charlotte Linlin (Big Mom) est mentionnée mais n'apparaît pas physiquement dans ce chapitre. Hody Jones est également mentionné dans le contexte des esclavesévadés mais n'est pas présent directement. La scène des pirates évadés dans le Nouveau Monde est brève. Le combat Nami vs Luffy/Zoro/Sanji est comique plutôt que réel. L'arc est Fish-Man Island, pas East Blue Saga — le scraper semble mal catégoriser.

title: The Hero Hat
summary: The mermaid dancers from the Mermaid Cafe ask permission to see the Straw Hats off which they are granted by Madame Shyarly. The Minister of the Left introduces Nami to a new Log Pose from which she is able to tell which island is more dangerous. After a respectful and (in some cases) tearful farewell, the Straw Hat Pirates leave Fish-Man Island and head out to the New World. However, they are stopped for a brief moment by Shirahoshi, making a promise with her to take her to the surface the next time they meet. After they set sail once again, a fish-man child asks for a Straw Hat to play hero, but is told that there are none for sale. On the way to the surface, the Straw Hat Pirates remember and re-establish their dreams and prepare to enter the New World.

taxonomy.revelation_description: The Minister of the Left introduces Nami to a new Log Pose capable of indicating the relative danger level of New World islands, marking a key navigational upgrade for entering the New World.
taxonomy.tagger_notes: The résumé is clear but brief. Straw Hats count set to 9 assuming all post-timeskip crew members are present (Luffy, Zoro, Nami, Usopp, Sanji, Chopper, Robin, Franky, Brook). arc_ends is True as the Fish-Man Island arc concludes with the crew's departure. The 'fish-man child asking for a straw hat' likely inspired the chapter title 'The Hero Hat'. revelation_major flagged for the new Log Pose mechanics, which is lore-significant for New World navigation. No fights occur in this farewell chapter.

title: Gam
summary: On the way to the surface, Nami is taking a bath while Luffy and the others start fishing. They catch a large fish which is eaten by another larger fish which is in turn eaten by an even bigger sea creature. After catching it they get too close to the White Strom and get caught in it. Shortly after that they hit a pod of Island Whales and stop. Brook is overwhelmed and confused by his joy, thinking one of the whales to be Laboon. He soon calms down, begins playing Binks' Sake, and because they like the music, one of the whales decides to give the crew a ride to the surface on its back. They soon reach the surface, where they are sent flying and can clearly see the conditions of the New World.

taxonomy.tagger_notes: Chopper est absent du résumé malgré son appartenance à l'équipage — possiblement présent en arrière-plan mais non mentionné. Le White Strom est un tourbillon naturel, non un personnage. Les Island Whales sont des créatures, dont l'une transporte le Sunny vers la surface. La scène emotionnelle de Brook avec Laboon (confondant l'un des baleines avec son vieil ami) est le point fort émotionnel du chapitre. Arc identifié comme transition entre Fishman Island et New World.

title: Punk Hazard
summary: The Straw Hats arrive in an agitated sea where the deep sea fish they just caught had been burnt in the water. Soon after their Den Den Mushi begins to cry, and despite Robin warning them about it possibly being a marine trap, Luffy answers it. The distress call turns out to be genuine and the person calling is in urgent need for salvation from a hostile samurai, but he is stabbed and the call ends. Luffy, and three others that were chosen by lottery (Zoro, Robin and Usopp) sail over the sea of flames with assistance from Nami to Punk Hazard. There, after ignoring the huge warning on the gates, they enter the island and see the melted ruins of a former base of the World Government. They are then confronted by a dragon who asks who they are.

taxonomy.revelation_description: Punk Hazard is revealed as a ruined former World Government base with a sea of flames and a living dragon, hinting at mysterious past experiments or events on the island.
